falklands.name: Tussipit (Falklands)
falklands.fact: The Falkland Islands have their own pipit, the correndera pipit, a streaky ground-nesting songbird that is a different species from the South Georgia pipit.

falklands.name: Hopperlet (Southern)
falklands.fact: The rockhoppers of the Falklands are southern rockhoppers; the birds of Tristan and Gough are now classed as a separate species, the northern rockhopper.

bermuda.name: Duneskink (Bermuda)
bermuda.fact: Bermuda's only native land reptile is the Bermuda skink, also called the rock lizard, and it is found nowhere else.

anole.name: Duneskink (Anole)
anole.fact: Anoles are small Caribbean lizards that flick out a bright throat fan, called a dewlap, to signal to rivals and mates; Montserrat has its own species, found nowhere else.

land_crab.name: Pinchkin (Land Crab)
land_crab.fact: Blue land crabs live in burrows well inland and walk down to the sea once a year to release their eggs.

camp.name: Herdlet (Camp)
camp.fact: Sheep far outnumber people in the Falklands, and the country outside Stanley is known as Camp.

mountain_chicken.name: Croakle (Mountain Chicken)
mountain_chicken.fact: The mountain chicken is a giant frog found on Montserrat and Dominica, and a deadly fungus has wiped out most of the wild ones.

red_footed.name: Gannetling (Red-footed)
red_footed.fact: Little Cayman's Booby Pond is home to a large colony of red-footed boobies, one of the biggest in the Caribbean.

masked.name: Gannetling (Masked)
masked.fact: Ascension's feral cats were cleared by 2006, and seabirds such as masked boobies have been returning to nest on the main island.

kelp.name: Chipgull (Kelp Gull)
kelp.fact: Kelp gulls are the gulls of the southern oceans, and they breed on South Georgia and along the Antarctic Peninsula.

laughing.name: Chipgull (Laughing Gull)
laughing.fact: The laughing gull is named for its call, and in summer it wears a black hood on its head.

yellow_legged.name: Chipgull (Yellow-legged)
yellow_legged.fact: Round the Mediterranean the common big gull is the yellow-legged gull, and it has yellow legs where a British herring gull has pink ones.

fur_seal.name: Pupplash (Fur Seal)
fur_seal.fact: South Georgia is home to most of the world's Antarctic fur seals, which were nearly wiped out by sealers in the 1800s.

sea_lion.name: Selklet (Sea Lion)
sea_lion.fact: The Falklands have southern sea lions, which were hunted hard in the 1800s and have been slow to recover.

henderson.name: Petrelash (Henderson Petrel)
henderson.fact: The Henderson petrel breeds only in the Pitcairn Islands, mostly on Henderson Island.

wilsons.name: Petrelash (Wilson's)
wilsons.fact: Wilson's storm petrels breed on Antarctic coasts and sub-Antarctic islands, then fly north to feed in the northern summer.

brookei.name: Peregrin (Mediterranean)
brookei.fact: Gibraltar's peregrines are the Mediterranean subspecies, Falco peregrinus brookei, and they nest on the Rock's cliffs.

black_kite.name: Kitelet (Black Kite)
black_kite.fact: Each spring and autumn tens of thousands of raptors, many of them black kites, cross the Strait of Gibraltar to avoid a long sea crossing.

fruit_bat.name: Flittermouse (Fruit Bat)
fruit_bat.fact: Cyprus is home to the Egyptian fruit bat, the only fruit bat in Europe.

monastery_cat.name: Wildkit (Monastery Cat)
monastery_cat.fact: Legend says St Helena sent cats to Cyprus in the 4th century to deal with snakes, and the Monastery of St Nicholas of the Cats on the Akrotiri peninsula still keeps them.
